summary: Memoization saves the result of each function call so the same input is never computed twice. It turns naive recursive Fibonacci from exponential time into linear time.
notes: if n in memo: return memo[n] is the lookup that skips repeated work.
@functools.cache stores results in a dictionary for you. cache_info() shows hits and misses.
functools.cache only works when every argument is hashable, such as int or str.
pitfall: Putting memo = {} inside fib_memo creates a new empty dictionary on every call, so nothing is ever saved and the function is as slow as the naive version.
